extracted.intended_audience: Mathematics Stack Exchange users asking about the presentation or formulation of mathematical proofs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for asking and answering questions about the presentation, clarity, and formulation of mathematical proofs on Math.SE (not for requesting someone to produce a proof). Focuses on what to ask about proof structure, detail, sufficiency, and readability, and how to tag such questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: questions about formulation/presentation of a proof
rubrics_metrics.description: For questions about the formulation of a proof. Questions with this tag are about the presentation of a mathematical proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical acceptable questions concern the presentation aspects of proofs (structure, order of arguments, clarity), rather than purely mathematical content or problem-solving technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag usage: not to be the only tag
rubrics_metrics.description: This tag should not be the only tag for a question and should not be used to ask for a proof of a statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always pair proof-writing with one or more subject-specific tags (e.g., abstract-algebra, real-analysis) so the question is grounded in the relevant mathematical area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: not for asking someone else to write a proof
rubrics_metrics.description: This tag is not for asking someone else to write a proof for you, or for how to answer some question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use this tag for homework-style 'please prove X' or 'I don't know how to begin' requests; such questions are off-topic for proof-writing usage. Example disallowed phrasing: 'My professor asked me to prove the Pythagorean theorem and I don't know how to begin.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Level of detail: whether to include specific mathematical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Should I include [x-mathematical detail] at [y-part of this proof]?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions may ask about the appropriate level of technical detail at particular steps or parts of a proof (e.g., when to expand a step, when to cite a known result, what to leave as an exercise). Aim to show the relevant excerpt and ask about the local level of detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency/validity: is the proof adequate?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the following a sufficient proof of [x-mathematical tidbit]?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions can request evaluation of whether a presented proof is complete and logically sufficient; provide the proof text and the statement being proved so reviewers can check for gaps, unjustified steps, or missing cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and readability: improving flow and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: I have written the following proof, could I somehow improve it, does it have good flow/can I improve readability?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask for suggestions on organization, exposition, notation, sentence structure, and how to make the argument more accessible. Include the current write-up and indicate the target audience/level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended pairing with subject-specific tags
rubrics_metrics.description: This tag is intended for use along with other, more 'mathematical' tags. A question about the writing of a proof in abstract algebra, for example, should have abstract-algebra as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the specific field tag(s) so answers can consider field-specific conventions and standard results that can be cited rather than reproved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Can be used with proof-verification tag
rubrics_metrics.description: This tag can be used along with the [proof verification] tag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both when you want both verification of correctness and advice on presentation; clarify whether you seek correctness checking, exposition improvement, or both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pointer to external solution-writing guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: See here for a useful set of guidelines for writing a solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tag wiki links to a separate set of guidelines for writing solutions; consult those for more comprehensive advice on structure, style, and expectations when presenting solutions.
